newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Nokia says Swedes to buy one mln mobiles in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Nokia says Swedes to buy one mln mobiles in 1997.

text.p: Finnish telecommunications group Nokia Oy said on Wednesday it expected Swedes to buy over one million mobile telephones in 1997.

"Today it is estimated that around 28 percent of Swedes have mobile telephones. In 1997 this figure will exceed 35 percent," Mads Winblad, managing director of Nokia Mobile Phones Scandinavia, said in a statement.
The high demand for mobile telephones in 1997 was partly due to the fact that in 1996 50 percent or more of mobile phone were bought to replace old phones, not new buys.
"Mobile telephones have become an integrated part of Swedish society, which means that more and more Swedes see the possibilities and advantages with mobile telephones," Nokia said in a statement.
"In the Stockholm region almost 50 percent of the population have mobile telephones."
Strong competition between operators and services was creating a more consumer-friendly mobile telephone market.

"The market between mobile telephone operators is also marked by strong competition which is stimulating the market. New and better mobile telephones are constantly being launched on the market," Nokia said.
The company said fewer women had mobile telephones than men but a larger number of women were now buying them.
More and more elderly people and young people were also buying mobile telephones, the first group for safety reason and the second because they tended to move around a lot.
Winbald would not give any forecasts for how many subscribers there would be in 1997.
"I am speaking only about the number of mobile telephones sold. Only operators can comment on the number of subscribers," Winblad said.
